shortcut_name: connected n−1-edge graph is a tree
evidence: deepseek-v4-flash builds an adjacency list and uses a terminal-aware DFS; gpt-oss-120b builds parent and parent-edge arrays with an iterative traversal. Both rely on pruning edges whose component contains no terminal.
affordance_in_statement: The facility is completely integrated, meaning it is possible to route components between any two workstations via some sequence of belts. ... the number of conveyor belts m is always exactly one less than the number of workstations (m = n − 1). ... The conveyor belts form the completely integrated structure described above.
removal_suggestion: There is no valid wording-only removal: connectedness together with the immutable condition m = n − 1 mathematically forces the input graph to be a tree. Defeating this reduction would require changing the graph constraints or the task.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Uses the forced tree structure and performs a terminal-aware subtree DFS, retaining exactly edges needed to connect quality-control stations.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Uses the forced tree structure with parent and parent-edge arrays, then aggregates whether each subtree contains a quality-control station.

common_affordance: The graph is necessarily a tree because it is connected and has exactly n − 1 edges.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: Its DSU/heap-based generic graph approach does not correctly apply the terminal-subtree pruning criterion required for the unique tree paths.
Its marked-wrong implementation does not correctly identify and sum precisely the edges lying in the minimal subtree spanning all terminals.

recommended_edit: No permissible edit can defeat all surviving models: the shared reduction is an unavoidable consequence of immutable input constraints and the connectivity guarantee.
